rationale: Zero-ask-approver regression check of f72803bb in the spec-contract-fidelity territory. THE FIX'S CORE IS FAITHFUL: (1) the corrected protocol (tip-seeded snapshot; commit-tree -> expected-old-tip update-ref -> index-only mixed reset) stays inside OQ-1(a)'s charter, leaves AC-6/AC-7(i) fixtures intact (bead 6 step 6 unchanged), and the expected-old-tip refusal on a CONCURRENT tip move is exactly AC-7(i)-consistent — the subsequent stale-SHA block is manufactured by the concurrent actor's commit, not complete's own, which is the behavior the spec wants; the three new red-on-revert legs (v)(vi)(vii) strengthen R4.2's artifact-confinement story. (2) The legacy-notice treatment is R3.2-compliant WITHIN R3.2's binding scope: R3.2 binds on the two R3.1 fixture routes, and under option 1 those routes (run with the new binary) write the v2 marker at preflight and keep stored==derived, so neither the mismatch warning nor the legacy notice fires there — AC-5(i)'s warning-absent arm holds. On the legacy-epic fixture (outside R3.2's fence) the hint's execution genuinely IMPROVES state — I re-derived the safety property: the legacy signature requires none-in_progress AND none-closed, so a genuinely-implementing epic can never match it and the #248 harm class (regressing real implementation) is unreachable by the reconciliation; goal (b)'s letter (hint execution never makes state worse on a reproducible state) is satisfied. (3) The fence restatement (zero-callers-outside-allowlist at bead 1, exactly-one at bead 2) is a correct phasing of the round-3 G5 sanction boundary. WHY RC ANYWAY — the G4 self-healing design quietly made the marker state SEMANTICS-DETERMINING for AC-5's own guard fixtures, and the plan does not pin it: AC-5's constructed backward case (stored implement, all children open) IS the legacy signature, and with repair phase now invoking EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 BEFORE its guard evaluates, a marker-ABSENT fixture makes repair reconcile-and-no-op instead of refuse — the AC-5(ii) refusal assertion and AC-5(viii)'s operator-path-still-refuses assertion never see the refusal they test, and AC-5(iv)'s direction-conditional retained warning never fires (the legacy notice fires instead, carrying the repair-phase line the AC's letter forbids for backward cases). Every one of those legs is satisfiable — but only on marker-PRESENT fixtures, and the plan must say so or an implementer writes tests the design fails. Second, my round-2 minor finding (recorded, unconsolidated) is now AMPLIFIED and still unaddressed: plan line 356 still claims 'exactly one sanctioned backward writer (release's sync)' while the delivered design has a second unforced backward-writing path — EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2's implement->plan relabel, now invoked from repair phase, release, next, and three preflights. The reconciliation is one sentence (it is a one-shot semantics TRANSLATION under a durable marker, not a lifecycle move, hence outside the sanction taxonomy) but its absence is now a live internal contradiction that the writer-inventory and AC-5(viii) implementers will trip over. Third, the new reset-failure recovery ('refuses with a recovery line naming the idempotent re-run') is in tension with the plan's own honest-scope paragraph: a reset failure occurs AFTER update-ref advanced the tip to C, so a plain re-run meets the panel stale-SHA gate (tip C != reviewed A) unless complete resumes — the plan must either specify resume detection (tip's tree == T -> skip to the sync-commit stage) or route that leg honestly to the 127 post-gate machinery like every other post-gate failure; as written the hinted recovery does not obviously work, which is the hint-honesty class this spec exists to close. All three are small, targeted plan edits; none impeaches the design itself, hence RC without hard_block.
concrete_changes_required: Pin the v2-marker state in AC-5's fixture constructions (MINOR but test-determining): state explicitly that the AC-5(ii), (iv), (v), and (viii) guard/warning fixtures construct marker-PRESENT states (so the backward-refusal and direction-conditional-warning paths are exercised), and that the marker-ABSENT stored-implement/all-open state is the LEGACY fixture exercising the notice + self-heal instead. Also classify the legacy notice explicitly as NOT a 'retained form of the phase-mismatch warning' for AC-5(iv) purposes (it is a replacement notice whose hinted command self-heals), so the AC-5(iv) test is written against the retained warning only. Without this, repair's new EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2-at-entry makes the AC-5(ii)/(viii) refusal assertions unsatisfiable on the naively-constructed fixture.

Reconcile the sanction count (MINOR, carried from round-2 finding R1-2-1, now amplified): plan line 356's 'exactly one sanctioned backward writer (release's sync)' contradicts EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2's unforced implement->plan relabel (invoked from repair phase, release, next, and the three preflights). Add the one-sentence classification — the v2 reconciliation is a one-shot semantics translation under a durable marker, not a lifecycle move under v2 semantics, and is therefore outside the sanction taxonomy the round-3 G5 sentence counts — or recount the writers.

Specify the reset-failure re-run semantics (MINOR): the materialization op's reset-failure leg promises 'a recovery line naming the idempotent re-run', but after update-ref the tip is at C != reviewed_head_sha, so a plain re-run meets the panel stale-SHA gate. Either specify the resume detection that makes the re-run idempotent in fact (e.g. tip commit's tree == T means materialization already landed -> proceed to the artifact-sync/merge stage) or scope the recovery to the spec-127 post-gate machinery as the honest-scope paragraph already does for other post-gate failures — the hinted command must actually work when executed (goal (b)'s principle, and R4.3's plain-re-run promise).

TRIVIAL (carried from round-2 R1-2-2): bead 2's Acceptance Criteria parenthetical still reads AC-5(iv) 'retains its safe final recovery line'; align it with the recorded direction-conditional disposition ('backward disagreements emit the bd show inspection line').

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE (G4 interaction): marker state now determines AC-5 guard-fixture semantics and is unpinned
findings.detail: AC-5's constructed backward case (stored implement, all lifecycle children open) is byte-identical to the legacy signature. With repair phase added to EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2's invocation sites, invoking repair on that state with the marker ABSENT reconciles (implement->plan + marker) and no-ops as consistent — it never refuses. The AC-5(ii) refusal leg, AC-5(viii)'s operator-refusal contrast, and AC-5(iv)'s direction-conditional retained warning are all satisfiable only on marker-PRESENT fixtures; the legacy notice (marker-absent branch) carries a repair-phase recovery line that a literal AC-5(iv) test would fail. One or two sentences pinning fixture marker state and the notice's classification close this.

findings.title: MISSED (round-2 R1-2-1, amplified): 'exactly one sanctioned backward writer' now has a second counterexample path
findings.detail: f72803bb did not touch the advisory-discharge paragraph (plan line 356). The G4 fix widened the gap: EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2's unforced implement->plan write is now reachable from repair phase, release, next, and three preflights. Prose-only (the mechanical fences — call-site enumeration on SanctionedDerivedSync, writer inventory — remain coherent), but a plan that miscounts its own backward writers invites a false writer-inventory or AC-5(viii) interpretation at implementation time.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE (G2): reset-failure 'idempotent re-run' recovery is unproven against the stale-SHA gate
findings.detail: After update-ref succeeds the tip is C; if the index-only reset then fails, the promised plain re-run hits the panel stale-SHA gate (C != reviewed_head_sha) — the exact confusing-block shape #186 describes, now hinted by the tool itself. Specify resume detection (tip tree == T -> materialization already landed) or route the leg to the 127 post-gate machinery per the honest-scope paragraph. The other failure leg (update-ref race) is correctly specified: nothing advanced, re-run re-measures, and a stale-SHA block there is the concurrent actor's commit tripping AC-7(i) as designed.

findings.title: Regression check passed on the rest of the fix, in this lens's territory
findings.detail: Tip-seeded snapshot and the never-touches-artifact/byte-identical legs keep R4.2's artifact story consistent and AC-6/AC-7(i) intact; the legacy-signature predicate cannot match a genuinely-implementing epic (requires none-in_progress AND none-closed), so the self-heal can never regress real implementation — goal (b) satisfied on the legacy fixture, and R3.2's binding fixture routes stay warning-free under option 1 (marker written at preflight, stored==derived throughout); spec approve remains outside the V2 invocation sites so AC-16's replay fixtures are unaffected; the bead-1/bead-2 fence phasing (zero-callers-allowlist, then exactly-one) delivers the round-3 G5 boundary; chunk 2's impl.go addition restores chunk/step consistency. Trigger-2 discharge, the (c)-only vacations, and the dead option-2 arms are untouched by this fix and stand as verified in rounds 1-2.
